newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee firms after intervention-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee firms after intervention-dealers.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against both the dollar and pound on Tuesday after central bank intervention on Monday, commercial banks forex dealers said.
The rupee was fixed at a mean commercial rate of 19.928 against the dollar from 20.008 on Monday. Against the pound, the rupee traded at a mean rate of 33.1950 from 33.2245 on Monday.
Forex dealers said the stronger rupee reflected a combination of central bank intervention on Monday and overnight weakening of the dollar in international markets.
"The central bank sold dollars in the interbank forex market on Monday mid afternoon at three cents below the prevailing interbank rate," one dealer said.
"This is the main reason for the stronger rupee today (Tuesday) but overnight weakening of the dollar abroad has also played a part in it," the dealer added.
The central bank intervention was also seen as providing support to the local currency after it weakened by four cents against the dollar on Monday on the back of international trends, dealers said.
They added hard currency demand from importers is very subdued at present.
